reference.label: Fibre cut
reference.definition: A physical break in a fibre span that prevents light from propagating past the break.
reference.example: Excavation cuts a span and the next amplifier detects no input light.

reference.label: Span loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in fibre-span attenuation that reduces downstream optical power without necessarily stopping all light.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 12 dB of loss and drives the downstream receiver below threshold.

reference.label: Disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: Disconnection of an optical connector or patch cord that removes light from the connected path.
reference.example: A technician removes the OMS-input jumper and the pre-amplifier loses input light.

reference.label: Contaminated connector
reference.definition: Contamination on an optical connector that introduces loss or reflections and degrades the signal.
reference.example: Dust on a line connector raises pre-FEC BER on the affected channel.

reference.label: Amplifier pump failure
reference.definition: Complete failure of an amplifier or its pump system that leaves the amplifier with no usable output.
reference.example: An in-line EDFA loses its pump and all traversing wavelengths disappear downstream.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: Partial loss of amplifier gain relative to its target, lowering output power across amplified channels.
reference.example: An EDFA delivers 3 dB less gain than provisioned and every wavelength leaves low.

reference.label: Amplifier noise-figure degradation
reference.definition: An increase in amplifier noise figure that reduces channel OSNR even when output power remains normal.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier holds target output power while all channels lose 3 dB of OSNR.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance that makes part of the optical band lower than the rest.
reference.example: Channels at the high-frequency band edge leave an EDFA 2 dB below mid-band channels.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive deterioration of an amplifier pump that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 121% of beginning-of-life current while gain remains on target.

reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: Failure of a transmitting optical laser that extinguishes its optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder laser stops emitting and the far-end receiver declares loss of signal.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: A card-level hardware failure that removes its traffic and valid monitoring functions.
reference.example: A muxponder loses power, drops its traffic, and stops updating telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local impairment that adds a decoding penalty without degrading the shared optical path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver develops excess noise while adjacent channels and the path remain normal.

reference.label: Transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmit-laser wear evidenced by rising bias current before eventual failure.
reference.example: Laser bias current climbs from 102% to 123% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Margin erosion
reference.definition: A gradual decline in an optical channel's remaining performance margin.
reference.example: A channel's estimated margin falls from 4 dB to 2 dB over several months.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: An unintended change in the attenuation applied by a WSS to one wavelength.
reference.example: A channel's WSS attenuation drifts upward by 2 dB and its output power becomes low.

reference.label: WSS passband offset
reference.definition: A frequency offset of a WSS passband from one channel's carrier, reducing signal quality while power may remain normal.
reference.example: A WSS passband shifts 4 GHz from the carrier and the receiver loses frame.

reference.label: WSS ingress-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a WSS ingress port that blocks all channels arriving on its associated ROADM degree.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS input fails while east-degree traffic continues normally.

reference.label: DGD increase
reference.definition: An increase in differential group delay on an optical path that impairs coherent reception.
reference.example: DGD rises during a fibre disturbance until the channel crosses its degrade threshold.

reference.label: Fast polarization event
reference.definition: A state-of-polarization change faster than the coherent receiver can track.
reference.example: Movement of an aerial fibre causes an SOP-rate spike and brief frame loss.

reference.label: Mechanical disturbance
reference.definition: A brief physical disturbance of fibre or patching that causes a transient optical loss excursion.
reference.example: Work on a patch panel produces a one-second received-power dip.

reference.label: Channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief OMS power excursion caused by adding or removing wavelength channels.
reference.example: Adding several wavelengths produces a short composite-power swing.

reference.label: Protection-switch interruption
reference.definition: A brief service interruption caused by selection changing between protection paths.
reference.example: An SNCP selector changes branches and the client loses traffic for several milliseconds.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that interrupts the ODUs traversing it.
reference.example: A fabric fault stops every cross-connected ODU and sends AIS downstream.

reference.label: OTN cross-connect misconnection
reference.definition: An incorrect OTN cross-connect that delivers an ODU to the wrong destination.
reference.example: ODU 7 is provisioned to the wrong client port and raises a trace mismatch.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a client interface or its optic that makes the associated client service unavailable.
reference.example: A 100GE client optic fails and its port drops the customer service.

reference.label: Instrument misreporting
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which an instrument reports an incorrect measurement value.
reference.example: A power monitor reports −30 dBm while an independent meter shows −8 dBm.

reference.label: Stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which a reported value stops updating and remains frozen.
reference.example: Received-power telemetry remains unchanged after the input fibre is disconnected.

reference.label: Unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: A wildcard for an unspecified fault earlier on the signal path that produces a downstream defect.
reference.example: Loss of signal is attributed to an upstream failure until the exact span or unit is identified.

reference.label: Unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: A wildcard for an unspecified failure in a server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: ODU unavailability is provisionally attributed to a server-layer failure.

reference.label: Optical signal lost
reference.definition: No expected optical signal is detected because power is below the receiver's detection threshold.
reference.example: The far-end receiver measures no channel power and declares optical loss of signal.

reference.label: Digital loss of signal
reference.definition: A digital receiver defect indicating that no valid digital signal can be detected.
reference.example: After input power collapses, the powered line receiver asserts dLOS.

reference.label: Low optical power
reference.definition: Optical signal or composite power is below its expected target while some light remains.
reference.example: A wavelength leaves a ROADM 4 dB below neighboring channels.

reference.label: OSC lost
reference.definition: The optical supervisory channel cannot be received on its span.
reference.example: A fibre cut causes the next amplifier site to stop receiving the span OSC.

reference.label: Power excursion
reference.definition: A brief optical-power dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Received power falls by 5 dB for one second during patch-panel movement.

reference.label: Low OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio is reduced by added noise or loss of signal quality.
reference.example: Every wavelength downstream of a degraded amplifier loses 2 dB of OSNR.

reference.label: Fast polarization change
reference.definition: State of polarization is changing at a rate beyond the receiver's tracking capability.
reference.example: SOP rate spikes above the coherent receiver's tracking limit.

reference.label: High DGD
reference.definition: Differential group delay is elevated enough to reduce coherent-receiver margin.
reference.example: The receiver reports 28 ps DGD during a fibre event.

reference.label: Filter penalty
reference.definition: Signal-quality loss caused by spectral narrowing or misalignment, often with normal measured power.
reference.example: A narrowed 50 GHz passband clips a 400G signal while channel power remains normal.

reference.label: Receiver penalty
reference.definition: A receiver-local quality impairment that does not propagate along the optical path.
reference.example: One receiver reports high pre-FEC BER while another copy of the same signal remains clean.

reference.label: Unit down
reference.definition: A unit is nonfunctional, carries no traffic, and provides no valid monitoring data.
reference.example: A failed card delivers no traffic and its performance counters stop updating.

reference.label: Traffic alarms masked
reference.definition: A dominant equipment alarm suppresses or obscures subordinate traffic alarms.
reference.example: A card-failure alarm masks individual OTU and ODU alarms from the card.

reference.label: OTU frame lost
reference.definition: A line receiver cannot acquire or maintain valid OTU frame alignment.
reference.example: Light remains present, but severe impairment prevents OTU frame recovery.

reference.label: OTU signal degraded
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors exceed the degrade threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER reaches 1×10^-4 and signal-degrade is asserted without frame loss.

reference.label: Errored seconds
reference.definition: One-second intervals in which at least one countable transmission error occurs.
reference.example: A 15-minute interval contains 18 errored seconds.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An alarm-indication signal carried downstream on an ODU to mark payload unavailable because of an upstream defect.
reference.example: OTU frame loss causes ODU-AIS to be inserted on every contained ODU.

reference.label: OTU backward defect indication
reference.definition: A backward indication sent toward the transmitting OTU endpoint after a receive-side defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses OTU frame sends OTU-BDI to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: ODU misrouted
reference.definition: An ODU is delivered to an endpoint other than its intended destination.
reference.example: An ODU intended for client port A appears at client port B.

reference.label: Client service down
reference.definition: The client service is unavailable in the affected direction.
reference.example: Failure of a client optic interrupts the associated 100GE service.

reference.label: Client service hit
reference.definition: A short client-service interruption rather than a sustained outage.
reference.example: Protection switching causes a several-millisecond traffic interruption.

reference.label: Pump-current ageing indication
reference.definition: Observed amplifier pump current is rising as control maintains the configured gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises to 118% while amplifier gain remains constant.

reference.label: Laser-bias ageing indication
reference.definition: Observed transmit-laser bias current is rising as output power is maintained.
reference.example: Laser bias rises steadily from 102% to 116% over six months.

reference.label: Margin decline
reference.definition: The measured or estimated performance margin of a channel is slowly decreasing.
reference.example: Receiver-estimated margin falls from 4 dB to 2 dB over a year.

reference.label: No amplifier output with input present
reference.definition: An amplifier has detectable input light but produces no detectable output light.
reference.example: Input power is −8 dBm while output power is below detection.

reference.label: Amplifier gain out of range
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differs materially from its provisioned target.
reference.example: Measured gain is 16.5 dB against a 19 dB target.

reference.label: Normal optical power
reference.definition: Measured optical power remains within its expected range despite a possible quality impairment.
reference.example: Channel power stays at −2 dBm although filter misalignment raises BER.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM blocking
reference.definition: All wavelengths arriving through one failed WSS ingress are prevented from passing the ROADM.
reference.example: Every west-arriving wavelength is blocked while other degrees remain operational.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver, either instantaneously or in performance bins.
reference.example: The receiver reports an average power of −11.2 dBm for the last 15-minute interval.

reference.label: Line errored-seconds count
reference.definition: A performance counter of errored seconds on a line interface, commonly accumulated in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: ES-15 records seven errored seconds in the current bin.

reference.label: Estimated OSNR
reference.definition: Per-channel OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver's DSP.
reference.example: The coherent receiver estimates channel OSNR at 18.5 dB.

reference.label: OCM OSNR
reference.definition: Per-channel OSNR measured by an optical channel monitor at a ROADM.
reference.example: The ROADM OCM reports 19 dB OSNR for channel 37.

reference.label: Pre-FEC BER
reference.definition: Bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction at a coherent receiver.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER rises from 1×10^-6 to 2×10^-4 as margin erodes.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay estimated for a coherent optical signal.
reference.example: The receiver DSP reports DGD of 28 ps.

reference.label: SOP rate
reference.definition: The measured rate at which a signal's state of polarization changes.
reference.example: SOP rate exceeds the receiver's tracking threshold during fibre movement.

reference.label: Laser bias percentage
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: Laser bias reads 121% of beginning-of-life current.

reference.label: Amplifier input power
reference.definition: Total optical power across all channels at an amplifier input.
reference.example: Amplifier input power falls from −6 dBm to −10 dBm after added span loss.

reference.label: Amplifier output power
reference.definition: Total optical power across all channels at an amplifier output.
reference.example: The amplifier reports +17 dBm composite output power.

reference.label: Pump-current percentage
reference.definition: Amplifier pump drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: Pump current reaches 122% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength by an optical channel monitor.
reference.example: The OCM reports channel 37 at −5.8 dBm and channel 38 at −2.1 dBm.

reference.label: Client errored-seconds count
reference.definition: A client-side counter of errored seconds, commonly accumulated in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: The current client interval contains 12 errored seconds.

reference.label: Client unavailable-seconds count
reference.definition: A client-side counter of unavailable seconds, commonly accumulated in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: A five-minute outage adds 300 client unavailable seconds.

reference.label: Alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor that raises status or alarms without exposing a numerical measurement.
reference.example: An OSC receiver reports only received or not-received status.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An erbium-doped fibre amplifier used to amplify the multiplexed optical line signal.
reference.example: An EDFA amplifies all wavelengths traversing an optical span.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier installed at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A booster raises the multiplexed signal to its configured launch power.

reference.label: In-line amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier installed at an intermediate site between fibre spans.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier compensates loss between two long-haul spans.

reference.label: Pre-amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier installed at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier boosts incoming channels before terminal reception.

reference.label: Coherent line interface
reference.definition: A coherent interface that transmits and receives one optical channel.
reference.example: A coherent line interface terminates a 400G wavelength.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: A line-interface device that maps a client signal directly onto an optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder carries one 400G client over one coherent wavelength.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: A line-interface device that aggregates multiple client signals onto an optical line signal.
reference.example: A muxponder combines client services into a 400G wavelength.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card providing an OTN optical line interface and OTU or ODU processing.
reference.example: An OTN line card terminates an OTU and exposes its contained ODUs.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: A wavelength-routing optical node that uses WSS elements to switch channels among degrees.
reference.example: A ROADM routes channel 21 east and channel 22 south.

reference.label: WSS degree module
reference.definition: The wavelength-selective switch module serving one directional degree of a ROADM.
reference.example: The west-degree WSS receives and routes all wavelengths arriving from the west.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: A switch containing a fabric that cross-connects ODUs between interfaces.
reference.example: An OTN switch cross-connects an ODU from a line card to a client port.

reference.label: Client port
reference.definition: A client-facing interface that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GE client port maps customer traffic into an ODU.

reference.label: Optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when an optical-channel receiver detects no expected channel light.
reference.example: OCH_LOS is raised after an upstream fibre cut removes the wavelength.

reference.label: OTU loss-of-frame alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when a receiver loses OTU frame alignment.
reference.example: OTU_LOF is raised with light present after severe filter misalignment.

reference.label: OTU signal-degrade alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when OTU errors exceed the configured degradation threshold.
reference.example: OTU_SD is raised when pre-FEC BER crosses its threshold.

reference.label: OTU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the remote OTU endpoint returned a backward defect indication.
reference.example: The transmitter reports OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses frame.

reference.label: Transmit-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm identifying a detected fault in a transmit laser or its drive circuitry.
reference.example: EQPT_TX_FAIL is raised when laser drive is present but no optical output is detected.

reference.label: Card-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm identifying an internal card hardware failure.
reference.example: A failed card power rail raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: High laser-bias alarm
reference.definition: An ageing alarm raised when transmit-laser bias exceeds its configured life threshold.
reference.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH is raised when bias reaches 123% of beginning-of-life current.

reference.label: Amplifier input-loss alarm
reference.definition: An amplifier alarm indicating that incoming composite optical power is absent.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier raises AMP_INPUT_LOS after the preceding span is cut.

reference.label: OMS input-loss alarm
reference.definition: A pre-amplifier alarm indicating loss of light at the OMS input.
reference.example: OMS_LOS_P is raised when the OMS-input jumper is removed.

reference.label: OSC loss alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the optical supervisory channel is not received on a span.
reference.example: OSC_LOS is raised at the next site after a span cut.

reference.label: Amplifier failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that an amplifier has input light but produces no output.
reference.example: AMP_FAIL is raised after an EDFA pump stops with valid input power present.

reference.label: Amplifier gain-out-of-range alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when measured amplifier gain differs excessively from its target.
reference.example: AMP_GAIN_OOR is raised for 16 dB measured gain against a 19 dB target.

reference.label: Amplifier pump end-of-life alarm
reference.definition: An alarm raised when amplifier pump current exceeds its configured ageing threshold.
reference.example: AMP_PUMP_EOL is raised at 121% pump current.

reference.label: Client signal-fail alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that client traffic is unavailable at a client port.
reference.example: CLIENT_SF is raised after a fabric failure stops the port's ODU.

reference.label: ODU AIS receive alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating receipt of ODU alarm-indication signal at an ODU termination.
reference.example: ODU_AIS appears at the client port after upstream OTU frame loss.

reference.label: ODU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating receipt of backward defect indication from the remote ODU endpoint.
reference.example: ODU_BDI is reported when the remote ODU termination detects a trail defect.

reference.label: ODU trace-mismatch alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace does not match the expected identity.
reference.example: ODU_TIM is raised when a misconnected ODU carries another circuit's trace.

reference.label: Protection-active alarm
reference.definition: A state alarm indicating that traffic is selected from the protection rather than working path.
reference.example: PROT_ACTIVE appears after SNCP selects a clean protection ODU.

reference.label: Protection-unavailable alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that no defect-free protection branch is available.
reference.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when both working and protection ODUs are defective.

reference.label: Port-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm identifying failure of a client port or its optic.
reference.example: A dead client transceiver raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN fabric failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm identifying failure of an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: The switch raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL when it stops forwarding traversing ODUs.

reference.label: Single optical channel
reference.definition: Exactly one optical wavelength channel, excluding neighboring channels.
reference.example: A failed transmit laser removes only its associated wavelength.

reference.label: All multiplexed channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength sharing the affected multiplexed signal or common optical element.
reference.example: A dead in-line amplifier removes all channels traversing it.

reference.label: Subset of channels
reference.definition: More than one but not all channels in a multiplexed optical signal.
reference.example: Gain tilt leaves only the high-frequency edge channels low.

reference.label: One ROADM degree ingress
reference.definition: All channels arriving through one directional WSS ingress of a ROADM.
reference.example: Failure of the north-degree ingress blocks every channel arriving from the north.

reference.label: This receiver only
reference.definition: The individual receiving function under examination, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: Only one receiver records errors while another receiver of the same signal remains clean.

reference.label: Every traversing ODU
reference.definition: Every ODU cross-connected through the affected OTN switch or fabric.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupts every ODU traversing the switch.

reference.label: One ODU
reference.definition: A single ODU trail rather than all ODUs on a carrier or switch.
reference.example: A misconnection delivers one ODU to the wrong destination.

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The particular customer-facing service carried by the associated port and ODU path.
reference.example: A client-port failure affects its 100GE service.

reference.label: Unit itself
reference.definition: The equipment unit as an object, distinct from the traffic it carries.
reference.example: A health alarm applies to the amplifier card itself.

reference.label: Current unit
reference.definition: The local equipment unit that reports or exhibits the condition.
reference.example: Pump current is measured on the amplifier currently raising the alarm.

reference.label: Current port
reference.definition: The specific local interface that reports or experiences the condition.
reference.example: The equipment alarm identifies client port 3.

reference.label: Upstream span
reference.definition: The fibre span immediately preceding the current unit in the direction of signal flow.
reference.example: A break on the upstream span removes the amplifier's input light.

reference.label: Upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The nearest amplifier before the span feeding the current unit.
reference.example: Failure of the upstream amplifier causes input loss at the next site.

reference.label: OMS input
reference.definition: The input connection of the optical multiplex section at a receiving amplifier or node.
reference.example: Removing the patch at the OMS input causes immediate light loss.

reference.label: Upstream on the path
reference.definition: Any earlier point on the signal path capable of causing the downstream observation.
reference.example: Receiver loss of signal may originate from any upstream fibre, amplifier, or ROADM.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting toward the local receiver.
reference.example: OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the channel transmitted by the local unit.
reference.example: A local laser failure is observed as signal loss at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Either client endpoint
reference.definition: Either client-port termination of the service under consideration.
reference.example: Failure of the client optic at either endpoint can interrupt the service.

reference.label: OTN switch on the ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect traversed by the service's ODU path.
reference.example: A misconnection at an OTN switch sends the ODU to the wrong client.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route used under normal protected-service operation.
reference.example: A defect on the working ODU path causes selection of protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route available to protect the service.
reference.example: The selector chooses the protection ODU after the working copy develops AIS.

reference.label: Active ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU route currently selected to carry the protected service.
reference.example: After switching, the protection branch becomes the active ODU path.

reference.label: Baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring available by default, including alarms and standard performance counters.
reference.example: An operator reads alarms and 15-minute errored-second bins without an optional licence.

reference.label: Power monitoring
reference.definition: Optional monitoring that exposes optical input, output, or received-power measurements.
reference.example: The power option enables graphing of amplifier input power.

reference.label: Optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring that provides per-channel power and OSNR at optical channel monitors.
reference.example: An OCM compares power and OSNR across all ROADM wavelengths.

reference.label: Advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring that exposes coherent-DSP quantities and equipment health currents.
reference.example: Advanced telemetry reports pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, laser bias, and pump current.

reference.label: Hard fault
reference.definition: An abrupt definitive failure that normally causes immediate traffic or signal loss.
reference.example: A fibre cut causing complete optical loss is a hard fault.

reference.label: Soft fault
reference.definition: A degradative impairment in which traffic may continue with reduced quality or margin.
reference.example: A noise-figure increase causing low OSNR is a soft fault.

reference.label: Incipient fault
reference.definition: A slow warning trend that precedes likely failure while traffic remains usable.
reference.example: Rising laser bias before transmitter failure is an incipient fault.

reference.label: Transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less rather than a persistent fault.
reference.example: A one-second power dip during fibre movement is transient.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: The highest alarm-impact class for immediate major service or capacity loss.
reference.example: A switch-fabric failure affecting all ODUs is classified Critical.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: A high alarm-impact class for significant service or equipment impairment.
reference.example: Failure of one client port and its service is classified Major.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: A lower alarm-impact class for a condition needing attention without major current service loss.
reference.example: An early laser-bias warning with traffic intact is classified Minor.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported state or measurement that does not itself raise an alarm.
reference.example: A gradual margin decline may be visible in telemetry but not alarmed.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, ODU-AIS is sent downstream on contained ODUs and OTU-BDI is returned to the transmitter.
reference.example: A receiver losing OTU frame inserts AIS on its tributary ODUs and sends BDI upstream.

reference.label: Per-site OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and launches a separate OSC on the next span.
reference.example: OSC loss on span A–B does not prevent site B from originating the OSC for span B–C.

reference.label: SNCP receive-side selection
reference.definition: A protected service uses working and protection ODU copies with selection at the receiving client port.
reference.example: The receiver selects the clean protection ODU when the working ODU carries AIS.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM routing
reference.definition: A ROADM switches wavelengths independently, so an ingress-wide impairment persists on each routed channel.
reference.example: An OSNR penalty on west-ingress channels remains after some are routed east and others south.

reference.label: Pass-through behaviour
reference.definition: An arriving condition propagates through a unit without being removed or materially changed.
reference.example: An incoming OSNR penalty remains on a wavelength after amplification.

reference.label: Default handling behaviour
reference.definition: The fallback handling applied to an arriving condition when no more specific rule covers it.
reference.example: An unrecognized optical impairment is handled by the unit's default propagation rule.
